# Simpler sample-instrument behavior

## Scope and evidence rules

Owns `SURF-DEVICE-SIMPLER` in [the product inventory](../research/full-live-coverage-inventory.md).
This is a **partial draft**, not a released contract or a complete instrument family.
Requirements marked **D** describe the captured current Live 12 manual; **U** identifies
an unresolved outcome. Every D clause has **U exact 12.4.3 applicability**. Installed
schema/preset presence corroborates device identity and storage vocabulary only.
No application, original function or candidate was executed.

Canonical analysis and source pins: [sample instruments](../research/sample-instruments.md).
Generic chain/rack editing belongs to [device racks](device-racks.md), media/dependencies
to [project/media workflows](project-media-workflows.md), Set structure to
[live-set structure](live-set-structure.md), marker storage to [warp markers](warp-markers.md),
and automation ownership to [automation envelopes](automation-envelopes.md).
These links assign ownership; they do not resolve an interaction automatically.

## Requirements

### REQ-SIMPLER-001 — Load and replace sample (D)

Dropping a sample from the browser loads it. Dropping an audio clip from Session or Arrangement uses its start/end or loop-bounded region and retains its Warp Markers and warp settings. Dragging another sample or using sample Hot-Swap replaces the loaded sample. The precedence when clip start/end and loop bounds disagree is unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#simpler) (retained HTML line 1942); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-002 — Playback mode selection (D)

Expose Classic, One-Shot and Slicing modes. Classic is the documented initial mode with polyphonic playback and ADSR/looping; One-Shot is monophonic and has no looping; Slicing selects sample regions chromatically without modifying the original file. User defaults may replace initial settings.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#playback-modes) (retained HTML line 1984); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-003 — Classic region and percentage controls (D)

In Classic, absolute flags delimit the available region. Start and Length are percentages of that region. Length 50% selects half its duration. The Loop amount is active only while Loop is enabled. The precise Start/Length constraint and clamp rule at the region end remains unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#classic-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2014); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-004 — Classic looping, snap and fades (D)

Loop enables repeated playback while a note is held. Snap moves region/loop markers to zero crossings using the left channel of stereo samples; it does not guarantee a click-free right channel. Fade crossfades loop endpoints. The title-bar option selects constant-power (documented default) or linear loop fades; Fade is unavailable with Warp enabled (context-menu-options-for-simpler). Exact crossfade coefficients are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#classic-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2014); [manual §31.11.7](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#context-menu-options-for-simpler) (retained HTML line 2194); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-005 — Voice limits and repeated pitch (D)

Voices sets the simultaneous voice limit. When exceeded, the oldest voices are removed in favor of new voices. With Retrig enabled a sustaining copy of the same note is cut on its next trigger; with Retrig disabled same-note voices can overlap. A useful audible retrigger comparison requires Voices>1 and a long release. Exact stealing fade/tie ordering is unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#classic-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2014); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-006 — One-Shot Trigger, Gate and fade (D)

One-Shot uses absolute region flags, has no Loop/Length/Voices controls and is always monophonic. Trigger plays the sample after note release. Gate begins Fade Out at note release and reaches silence after its configured duration. In Trigger, Fade Out is placed before the sample-region end. Fade In starts at note onset. Endpoint rounding and fade curves are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.2](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#one-shot-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2032); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-007 — Automatic and manual slice creation (D)

Slice By Transient places slices according to detected transients; raising Sensitivity increases detected slices up to 64. Beat uses the selected beat division. Region divides the available region into equal durations. Manual adds no automatic slices; double-click within the region creates one. Exact detection thresholds and musical-boundary rounding remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.3](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#slicing-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2050); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-008 — Editing slice markers (D)

Automatic slice lines are blue and manually created lines white. Double-click an existing slice to delete; drag to move; double-click between slices to insert. In Transient mode Alt/Option-click toggles manual/automatic identity; manual slices survive Sensitivity changes. Marker collision and out-of-region movement rules remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.3](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#slicing-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2050); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-009 — Slice playback and fade extent (D)

Mono permits one slice; Poly allows multiple slices and exposes Classic Voices/Retrig behavior; Thru is monophonic and continues from the triggered slice through the rest of the region. Trigger/Gate behaves as in One-Shot. Mono/Poly fades span an individual slice; Thru fades span from the selected slice to region end. The lowest mapped note and overflow note behavior are not established here.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.1.3](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#slicing-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2050); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-010 — Warp mode interaction (D)

With Warp off, note pitch changes playback speed. Warp on follows Set tempo independently of the played pitch. Warp as sets a chosen musical duration. The ÷2 command doubles playback speed and ×2 halves it, as documented. Warp modes/marker storage belong to warp-markers.md; this clause provides no resampling, stretch or transient DSP oracle.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.2](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#warp-controls) (retained HTML line 2068); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-011 — Filter control availability (D)

Expose low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch and Morph with 12/24 dB slopes. Clean and OSR support every filter type; MS2/SMP/PRD are documented for low-pass/high-pass. Drive is present for low-pass/high-pass/band-pass with non-Clean circuits. Morph traverses low-pass → band-pass → high-pass → notch → low-pass and has context-menu snap choices. Cutoff accepts velocity, key, envelope and LFO modulation. Transfer functions and circuit nonlinearities are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.3](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#filter-1) (retained HTML line 2086); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-012 — Envelopes (D)

Amplitude, filter and pitch have ADSR controls, editable by values or graph handles. Attack reaches peak, Decay reaches Sustain, and note release begins Release toward zero. Pitch/filter envelope amounts govern their influence. Amplitude Loop/Trigger restarts after Decay when held, returning from sustain to initial over Time; Beat/Sync repeats after Rate. Precise envelope curves, clock alignment and mode-switch continuity remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.4](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#envelopes-2) (retained HTML line 2104); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-013 — Per-voice LFO (D)

LFO offers sine, square, triangle, descending/ascending saw and random; rate is 0.01–30 Hz or tempo divisions. Attack fades its depth in. Retrigger resets each new note to Offset; Offset has no effect while retrigger is off. Key scales rate by note pitch, with zero giving equal rate across voices. Destinations are Volume/Pitch/Pan/Filter. Random distribution and exact phase/sample math are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.5](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#lfo) (retained HTML line 2158); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-014 — Gain, output and stereo spread (D)

Sample Gain and final output Volume are separate gain stages; final Volume controls instrument output after the filter. The relative ordering of sample Gain and filter is unknown. Output Volume accepts velocity and LFO modulation. Pan accepts random and LFO modulation. Spread creates two detuned voices per note, one left and one right; its on/off decision is taken at Note On. Changing Spread later does not change whether that held note acquired the paired voices. Exact detune/pan/gain laws are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.6](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#global-parameters-1) (retained HTML line 2176); [manual §31.11.1.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#classic-playback-mode) (retained HTML line 2014); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-015 — Pitch reference, transpose and glide (D)

Without tuning or additional pitch modulation, C3 plays the sample at original pitch. Transpose spans ±48 semitones, Detune ±50 cents, and pitch bend sensitivity is documented as ±5 semitones. Glide is monophonic; Portamento is polyphonic; Time controls transition duration from the prior note pitch to the new one. MPE/tuning interactions and the exact glide trajectory are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.6](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#global-parameters-1) (retained HTML line 2176); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-016 — Non-destructive crop and reverse (D)

Crop retains only the Start/End-bounded sample region in a new copy. Reverse also creates a processed copy. The original sample bytes are preserved. Generated names, directories, repeated operation deduplication and failure atomicity are unknown; media ownership belongs to project-media-workflows.md.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.7](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#context-menu-options-for-simpler) (retained HTML line 2194); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-017 — Convert to Sampler and slice to racks (D)

Simpler → Sampler converts the preset. Sampler has no Simpler warp/slice functionality, so conversion of those modes carries no sound-equivalence promise. In Slicing, Slice to Drum Rack replaces this Simpler with a rack containing one pad per current slice. Slice to New MIDI Track instead adds a rack track and a clip playing slices in order. Generic rack/track/clip rules remain with device-racks.md and live-set-structure.md.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.7](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#context-menu-options-for-simpler) (retained HTML line 2194); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-018 — Sample management and normalization (D)

Manage Sample opens the File Manager for the sample; Show in Browser selects it there. Show in Finder/Explorer reveals the backing folder but is unavailable for official Ableton Pack samples. Normalize Volumes adjusts sample gain so the peak uses available headroom; exact peak scanning, gain rounding and silent-file handling remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.11.7](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#context-menu-options-for-simpler) (retained HTML line 2194); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-019 — Persistence and dependent media (U)

Exact save/reopen restoration of device modes, layer/slot assignments, markers, modulation, voice options and external media references is unknown. Stored fields in shipped content do not prove writer coverage, crash recovery or reload equivalence. Generic Set/media container behavior remains with live-set-structure.md and project-media-workflows.md.

Evidence: [lifecycle evidence gaps](../research/sample-instruments.md#unresolved-interactions); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-020 — Undo and redo (U)

Undo grouping, restoration of device/sample settings, marker/layer edits, generated files, conversion and routing changes are unknown. No promise of file deletion or resurrection is derived from a non-destructive operation.

Evidence: [lifecycle evidence gaps](../research/sample-instruments.md#unresolved-interactions); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-021 — Malformed or unavailable sample failure (U)

Acceptance of corrupt/truncated/unsupported audio, zero-length or missing samples, dependency resolution, out-of-range imported controls and failed allocation is unknown. No silence/no-crash or atomic rollback promise is invented.

Evidence: [lifecycle evidence gaps](../research/sample-instruments.md#unresolved-interactions); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-022 — Cancellation and voice teardown (U)

Cancel during sample replacement/import/conversion and remove or bypass while held notes play: resource cleanup, voice tail, pending-note handling and state restoration are unknown. Sample-rate changes, transport stop/restart and device reset have no established output oracle here.

Evidence: [lifecycle evidence gaps](../research/sample-instruments.md#unresolved-interactions); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SIMPLER-023 — DSP, scheduling and modulation fidelity (U)

Interpolation, filter/warp/stretch/saturation equations, gain/pan curves, modulation sums, random sequences, denormal/overload handling and sample-accurate note/control order are unknown. No numeric audio-error tolerance, performance bound or exact12.4.3 parity follows from manual descriptions.

Evidence: [lifecycle evidence gaps](../research/sample-instruments.md#unresolved-interactions); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

## Timing, state and comparison rules

Use fresh device state for each scenario; explicitly pin edition, mode, source hashes,
engine/sample rate, tuning, note duration and routing. MIDI note names use the manual’s
C3 convention; no numeric-note alias is inferred. Time/frequency/cent/semitone units
are those named in each clause. “Before/after” describes causal order, without an
invented audio-block latency. Endpoints and values are exact displayed choices;
float/audio comparisons require a separately supported tolerance. No sample-exact
DSP or timing oracle is supplied.

[Fixture definitions](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/fixtures.json)
pin three synthetic stereo PCM files with separated source bands. Their hashes and
known segment order identify test inputs, never Live output. `state` means compare
named visible states/counts/values exactly; `source-identity` distinguishes loaded
layers/regions, refusing ambiguous observations; `presence` tests only the named
continuation/termination or independence predicate, never waveform equality.
`unknown` records an observation without a pass/fail oracle. Cases with unavailable
third-party/official-Pack input stay unexecuted. All cases are plans and have not run.

# Sampler sample-instrument behavior

## Scope and evidence rules

Owns `SURF-DEVICE-SAMPLER` in [the product inventory](../research/full-live-coverage-inventory.md).
This is a **partial draft**, not a released contract or a complete instrument family.
Requirements marked **D** describe the captured current Live 12 manual; **U** identifies

## Requirements

### REQ-SAMPLER-001 — Multisample layers and focus (D)

Zone toggles a separate editor above Device View; Key/Vel/Sel select its range editor. Every contained sample is listed as a layer. Selecting a layer exposes it in the Sample tab. With Auto Select enabled, all layers eligible for the arriving note through key, velocity and selector zones are selected for that note duration. Simultaneous selection/ending-note tie behavior is unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.5](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#the-zone-tab) (retained HTML line 1554); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-002 — Key and velocity eligibility (D)

Each layer responds only within its key zone and Note On velocity zone. Newly imported key zones cover the full MIDI note range. Velocity zones span 1–127. The manual inconsistently describes full key coverage as “127” while naming C-2–G8; do not derive a 127-versus-128 endpoint rule from that wording. Zone-edge inclusivity and fade weighting are not independently resolved. See also velocity-zones.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.5.3](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#key-zones) (retained HTML line 1700); [manual §31.10.5.4](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#velocity-zones) (retained HTML line 1722); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-003 — Sample selector latch (D)

Each layer also has a 0–127 sample-select zone. A layer is eligible only if that zone overlaps the current selector. The selector affects availability at trigger time: moving it while a sample plays does not switch that playing voice to a different sample. Selector fade and exact boundary inclusivity are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.5.5](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-select-zones) (retained HTML line 1744); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

Zone edges resize ranges, zone bodies move them and upper corners set fades. Lin/Pow switches all zone fades between linear and constant-power modes. Range normalization on overlapping/crossed/zero-width edges, the exact gain law and endpoint rounding remain unknown; names alone do not prove sin/cos coefficients.

Layer menu supports Delete, Duplicate, Rename and sorting by name/key/velocity/selector in both directions. Select All With Same Range uses the currently active editor. Distribute Ranges Equally spans C-2–G8; Around Root Key allocates ranges around differing roots without overlaps, distributing equal-root layers evenly. Exact division remainder/tie rules are unknown.

### REQ-SAMPLER-006 — Round Robin modes (D)

With RR enabled, layers sharing the same key zone cycle by mode. Forward goes top→bottom and wraps; Backward bottom→top and wraps. Other excludes an immediate repeat; Random permits repeats. Reset Interval restarts at its chosen musical interval: Forward from top, Backward from bottom, and Other/Random from the sample first played. These are current manual clauses only; target applicability and interactions with unequal velocity/selector ranges, one eligible layer and stopped transport remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.5.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#round-robin-sample-playback) (retained HTML line 1598); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-007 — Per-layer sample controls (D)

Sample tab values generally apply to selected layer. Root Key sets its reference note; sample Detune spans ±50 cents; Volume ranges from attenuation to +24 dB; Pan controls that sample. Reverse and RAM/interpolation are explicitly global exceptions. Sample chooser changes edited layer. Exact root mapping under tuning is unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.6](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#the-sample-tab) (retained HTML line 1782); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-008 — Reverse and display-only controls (D)

Global Reverse plays from Sample End backwards through any active sustain loop toward Sample Start without generating a new file. Snap uses left-channel zero crossings for sample/loop points and does not ensure right-channel continuity. Vertical Zoom changes display only. B/M/L/R chooses displayed channels, without specifying any output-channel processing.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.6](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#the-sample-tab) (retained HTML line 1782); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-009 — Sample extent, sustain loop and Link (D)

Sample Start/End bound playback. Without an enabled loop, Sample End terminates playback even if the volume envelope continues; active sustain/release-loop behavior is the controlling exception, as specified here and in REQ-SAMPLER-010. With no sustain loop, playback ends at Sample End or completion of envelope release. Forward sustain loops return Loop End→Loop Start; back-and-forth loops reverse at both ends. With release mode Off they keep looping during volume-envelope release. Link makes effective Sample Start equal Loop Start, disabling but retaining the original Sample Start value for restoration when Link is disabled. Values can display samples or min:sec:ms.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.6.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-playback) (retained HTML line 1800); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-010 — Release modes and loop crossfades (D)

Release modes require active sustain looping. Release Enabled proceeds linearly toward Sample End on envelope release. Release Loop mode goes to Sample End then jumps to Release Loop start; back-and-forth release reverses between those points until the volume envelope ends. Crossfade is independently available for sustain/release loops with constant-power default or title-menu linear selection; loop Detune adjusts their pitch. Exact transition at a note-off coincident with a loop edge is unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.6.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-playback) (retained HTML line 1800); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-011 — Envelope stages and repetition (D)

Attack moves Initial→Peak; Decay Peak→Sustain; Release moves toward End on Note Off. Zero slope is linear; positive slopes move faster at the beginning, negative slopes faster at the end. Loop restarts after Decay, Beat/Sync after a musical Repeat interval; Sync aligns to song time. Trigger ignores Note Off. Velocity scales segments, not Beat/Sync beat-time. Exact curves/clock rounding remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.6.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-playback) (retained HTML line 1800); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

Interpolation is global, offering Normal, Good and Best quality. RAM is global and loads the entire multisample into RAM when enabled. Quality names provide no filter kernel or numeric fidelity contract. Allocation failure, streaming transition and memory-budget outcomes remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.6.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-playback) (retained HTML line 1800); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-013 — Modulation oscillator (D)

Each voice has an FM/AM modulation oscillator; its signal is not directly audible as an independent sound source. It has 21 waveform choices, modulation amount and velocity amount, plus an envelope. Fixed enables frequency Freq×Multi independent of input pitch; with Fixed off, Coarse/Fine are used. Exact waveforms, FM scaling and AM law remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.7.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#the-modulation-oscillator-osc) (retained HTML line 1888); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-SAMPLER-014 — Pitch envelope, zone shift and glide (D)

Pitch envelope affects sample and enabled modulation oscillator; Amount sets influence in semitones. Global Transpose/Detune act in semitones/cents. Key Zone Shift changes selection of sample layers while retaining played pitch. Spread creates two detuned voices per note. Glide is mono and Portamento poly, with Time defining transition duration. Pitch paths under alternate tuning and exact portamento law are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.7.2](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#the-pitch-envelope) (retained HTML line 1888); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

Its own filter envelope requires enable and nonzero Amount. Shaper offers Soft/Hard/Sine/4bit; the routing control selects shaper→filter or filter→shaper. Transfer functions and oversampling are unknown.

### REQ-SAMPLER-016 — Global articulation and voice control (D)

Volume envelope articulates the instrument; Time globally scales all envelope lengths and Time<Key varies that scaling by note pitch. Global Pan and random pan act across samples. Voices allows up to32 simultaneous voices. Retrigger reuses already-playing same-note voices instead of adding them. Voice stealing order, smoothing and any counting interaction with Spread remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.10.8.2](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#the-volume-envelope-and-global-controls) (retained HTML line 1906); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

## Timing, state and comparison rules

Use fresh device state for each scenario; explicitly pin edition, mode, source hashes,
engine/sample rate, tuning, note duration and routing. MIDI note names use the manual’s
C3 convention; no numeric-note alias is inferred. Time/frequency/cent/semitone units
are those named in each clause. “Before/after” describes causal order, without an
invented audio-block latency. Endpoints and values are exact displayed choices;
float/audio comparisons require a separately supported tolerance. No sample-exact
DSP or timing oracle is supplied.

[Fixture definitions](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/fixtures.json)
pin three synthetic stereo PCM files with separated source bands. Their hashes and
known segment order identify test inputs, never Live output. `state` means compare
named visible states/counts/values exactly; `source-identity` distinguishes loaded
layers/regions, refusing ambiguous observations; `presence` tests only the named
continuation/termination or independence predicate, never waveform equality.
`unknown` records an observation without a pass/fail oracle. Cases with unavailable
third-party/official-Pack input stay unexecuted. All cases are plans and have not run.

## Requirements

### REQ-IMPULSE-001 — Eight sample slots and editing focus (D)

Impulse has eight sample slots, loadable by dragging samples from browser/Session/Arrangement or per-slot Hot-Swap. Delete/Backspace removes loaded sample. Clicking a slot exposes that slot’s parameters. Hover controls offer play, solo, mute and Hot-Swap. Replacement settings retention and multi-drop distribution remain unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-slots) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-002 — Trigger mapping and editor labels (D)

Default C3 triggers the leftmost slot and remaining slots are mapped across the C3–C4 octave. The manual does not enumerate the six middle pitches; these remain unknown. With MIDI Editor Fold enabled, all eight slot labels appear even for keys without stored notes. Pitch/Scale MIDI effects may transpose/rearrange incoming triggers; those devices own transformation behavior.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-slots) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-003 — Parameters captured at new notes (D)

Per-sample parameter changes take effect for newly triggered notes, leaving playing notes unchanged; this also applies to those parameters changed by clip envelopes or automation. This clause does not establish the update timing of mute/solo/Link/global controls. Continuous curves and same-timestamp note/control ordering are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-slots) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-004 — Reciprocal link of slots7 and8 (D)

Slot8’s Link switch joins slots7/8 so triggering either stops playback of the other. It does not establish choke behavior among other slots. Note-simultaneity order and click suppression are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.1](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#sample-slots) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-005 — Start, transpose and stretch (D)

Start offsets playback up to100 ms from source beginning. Per-slot Transpose spans±48 semitones and accepts velocity/random modulation. Stretch spans−100%…100%; negative shortens and positive lengthens; Modes A/B select alternate algorithms, with velocity modulation of Stretch. Exact time/pitch transfer, endpoint−100 behavior and random laws are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.2](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#start-transpose-and-stretch) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-006 — Filter and saturation controls (D)

Per-slot filter offers type/Frequency/Resonance and velocity/random frequency modulation. Per-slot Saturator can be enabled/disabled and Drive changes input boost/distortion (saturator-and-envelope). Filter response, nonlinear shape, gain compensation and oversampling are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.3](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#filter) (retained HTML line 1040); [manual §31.7.4](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#saturator-and-envelope) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-007 — Trigger/Gate decay (D)

Per-slot Decay reaches a documented maximum10.0 seconds. Trigger begins decay with the note; Gate waits for Note Off before starting decay. This differs from Simpler’s One-Shot Trigger/Gate envelope. Sample-end truncation, envelope equation and minimum Decay are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.4](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#saturator-and-envelope) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

### REQ-IMPULSE-008 — Per-slot and global controls (D)

Each sample has Pan/Volume; Pan accepts velocity/random modulation and Volume velocity modulation. Global Volume and Transpose act on all samples; global Time controls both stretch and decay (global-controls). Exact global/per-slot composition, units/limits for global Time and whether a global change affects held voices are unknown.

Evidence: [manual §31.7.5](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#pan-and-volume) (retained HTML line 1040); [manual §31.7.6](https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-instrument-reference/#global-controls) (retained HTML line 1040); exact retained source locators in the [heading map](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/manual-headings.json).

## Timing, state and comparison rules

Use fresh device state for each scenario; explicitly pin edition, mode, source hashes,
engine/sample rate, tuning, note duration and routing. MIDI note names use the manual’s
C3 convention; no numeric-note alias is inferred. Time/frequency/cent/semitone units
are those named in each clause. “Before/after” describes causal order, without an
invented audio-block latency. Endpoints and values are exact displayed choices;
float/audio comparisons require a separately supported tolerance. No sample-exact
DSP or timing oracle is supplied.

[Fixture definitions](../../analysis/ableton-live-12.4.3/full-spec-v1/sample-instruments/fixtures.json)
pin three synthetic stereo PCM files with separated source bands. Their hashes and
known segment order identify test inputs, never Live output. `state` means compare
named visible states/counts/values exactly; `source-identity` distinguishes loaded
layers/regions, refusing ambiguous observations; `presence` tests only the named
continuation/termination or independence predicate, never waveform equality.
`unknown` records an observation without a pass/fail oracle. Cases with unavailable
third-party/official-Pack input stay unexecuted. All cases are plans and have not run.

## Documented distinctions preserved by the drafts

The manual locators are §31.7 `#impulse` (HTML line 1026), §31.10 `#sampler`
(1500) and §31.11 `#simpler` (1942); each requirement links the narrower heading.

- Simpler's modes, slice edits, warped clip import, voice stealing, sample
  replacement and non-destructive copy operations receive separate predicates.
  Warp mode names and “constant power” never become invented numerical algorithms.
- Sampler's eligibility combines key, velocity and selector zones. Changing the
  selector affects later triggers and does not switch a held voice. Global
  Reverse does not generate a file, unlike Simpler's Reverse command. Link
  retains the previous Sample Start value while substituting Loop Start.
- Current manual Sampler Round Robin clauses are useful D requirements, with
  specific Forward/Backward/Other predicates. The section's target-build
  applicability, reset state, unequal-zone interaction and single-layer Other
  behavior remain unresolved. A control name in another source would not settle
  all of those outcomes.
- Impulse's per-sample parameter changes are latched for later notes, including
  automation. This is not generalized to every global, mute, solo or Link
  control. Its Gate begins decay at Note Off; Simpler One-Shot Gate instead
  starts Fade Out then. The eight-slot mapping is not filled in from recollection.

These are documented facts/constraints, with target-version uncertainty. No
inference of sound-equivalence between the instruments is part of the packet.
